emma_support: FYI ticket #2341 — ACME reported a burst of 429s around 00:30 PST but the project quota tile shows ~75% remaining. Customer insists they didn't spike. Any ideas?

alex_sre: Can you paste the project/org + a sample request ID so I can check enforcement logs?

emma_support: project=acme-integration (proj_gtk7), org=acme-corp. sample req id: req_01H9X7A6. Customer log time: 2026-11-07T00:31:12-08:00 (PST). Attached CSV of token counts.

kai_eng: Quick note: our enforcement engine computes rolling windows anchored to UTC boundaries. The dashboard tiles are rendered using the org's timezone preference (PST) for the same windows. If a window alignment shifted (DST or timezone anchoring), totals can diverge enough to trigger enforcement while dashboard looks fine.

emma_support: Oh — DST was Nov 1 in customer region. Could that create a 1-hour misalignment?

kai_eng: Yup. Example repro I ran: when a customer's timezone is behind UTC, the dashboard shows the last hour in local time, but enforcement slides the rolling window relative to UTC. Small repeated bursts near the boundary can double-count across the two window definitions.

alex_sre: I pulled enforcement logs for req_01H9X7A6: 
```
[2026-11-07T08:30:52Z] ENFORCE hit org=acme-corp project=proj_gtk7 window_start=2026-11-07T08:00:00Z window_end=2026-11-07T09:00:00Z tokens=125432 threshold=125000 action=throttle
[2026-11-07T08:31:12Z] RAISED 429 req=req_01H9X7A6
```
Note logs are UTC. Dashboard tile query for customer (PST) returned tokens=99000 for what the UI labeled as "current hour". That lines up: enforcement window (UTC) had 125k and UI's local window had ~99k.

emma_support: So billing/invoice will match which one? Customer is worried invoice will show the bigger number.

nick_billing: Invoicing/metering uses the raw token ledger (UTC timestamps). So invoice numbers will match the enforcement ledger (UTC). Dashboard is just a UI aggregation layer and can show different windowing unless we normalize it.

kai_eng: Short-term options: 1) inform customer and offer temporary quota bump while we fix. 2) patch dashboard copy to show timezone/anchor info. 3) long-term: align dashboard aggregation to enforcement window semantics or make enforcement respect org timezone for project-level checks (needs design).

emma_support: Customer requested immediate action — they want outage credit and a short-term guardrail so they don't see more 429s.

alex_sre: I'll enqueue a temporary quota increase for acme-corp for 24h and add a canary rule to skip enforcement for small bursts during the next hour boundary. Filing bug RB-7896 (quota-window-anchor) and linking logs.

quota-bot: Created incident stub #RB-7896 and attached enforcement logs.

emma_support: I'll reply to the customer with the explanation (UTC vs org-local windowing), offer a 10% billing credit for the impacted window, and note we're working on the root fix.

nick_billing: Please also capture the CSV they attached into the billing ticket — we might need it if they dispute invoice lines.

kai_eng: FYI I created a small repro script to simulate the DST edge case (ran it against staging). Pseudocode: 
```
# rolling window aligned to UTC
now_utc = utcnow()
window_start = floor_to_hour(now_utc) - timedelta(hours=1)
count = sum(tokens where ts >= window_start and ts < now_utc)
```
Dashboard uses local tz floor: floor_to_hour(now_local). That mismatch causes overlapping/disjoint slices around DST/offset changes.

emma_support: Thanks. Keeping ticket open and will update once customer accepts the credit.

alex_sre: Follow-up items: (1) RB-7896 bug triage, (2) temp quota bump applied, (3) billing note + CSV saved. Marking as high-priority. :white_check_mark:

emma_support: Closing loop here — customer accepted 10% credit, and we scheduled a postmortem with eng to decide long-term fix. I'll paste the PM notes into the ticket. :thumbsup:
